svg.text: QuickBooks → OpenAccountants · bookkeeping-coding review [MOCK (set OA_MCP_TOKEN + QBO creds to go live)]
📒 Dell · $12,000 → 'Office Supplies' (Server and workstation hardware)
OpenAccountants → US bookkeeping / tax coding review (tier 1, signed off by Amir Pelinkovic (US lead))
⚠️ Capital asset expensed — should be capitalized (> $2,500 safe harbor)
$12,000 coded to 'Office Supplies'. Above the de-minimis safe harbor it should be a Fixed Asset and depreciated (or elect §179/bonus), not expensed.
📒 Joe's Grill · $200 → 'Meals - 100%' (Client dinner)
OpenAccountants → US bookkeeping / tax coding review (tier 1, signed off by Amir Pelinkovic (US lead))
⚠️ Business meals are 50% deductible — coded at 100%
Coded to 'Meals - 100%'. Move to a 50%-meals account so the deduction is limited correctly.
📒 Amazon · $800 → 'Office Expenses' (Owner personal headphones)
OpenAccountants → US bookkeeping / tax coding review (tier 1, signed off by Amir Pelinkovic (US lead))
⚠️ Personal expense in the business books — not deductible
Coded to 'Office Expenses'. Reclassify to Owner's Draw / distribution; it's not a deductible business expense.
📒 Apple · $1,500 → 'Office Supplies' (MacBook Air laptop)
OpenAccountants → US bookkeeping / tax coding review (tier 1, signed off by Amir Pelinkovic (US lead))
✅ Under the $2,500 de-minimis safe harbor — OK to expense
$1,500 tangible property; fine to expense rather than capitalize.
📒 Figma · $300 → 'Software Subscriptions' (Design tool subscription)
OpenAccountants → US bookkeeping / tax coding review (tier 1, signed off by Amir Pelinkovic (US lead))
✅ Coding looks fine
$300 to 'Software Subscriptions' — ordinary deductible business expense.
